c.tagline: Rumi's whirling-dervish city and Seljuk heart of Anatolia.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis are metered; hail on the street or book through BiTaksi or Uber, which dispatch licensed taxis. Fares are inexpensive by European standards.

emergency.note: 112 is Türkiye's single nationwide emergency number for police, ambulance and fire.

hood_desc: The historic core around the turquoise-domed Mevlana Museum, Rumi's tomb and Konya's spiritual heart, ringed by Seljuk mosques, madrasa museums, bazaars and the Semazen cultural center; the essential, walkable base for first-time visitors.

The green park-topped hill at the center of the old city, crowned by the 12th-century Alaeddin Mosque and encircled by tea gardens and tram stops; a pleasant, central spot minutes from the main sights.
Konya's modern northern district of wide boulevards, universities, shopping malls and newer hotels; more contemporary and business-oriented, well connected by tram to the historic center.
A relaxed, leafy suburb known for its vineyards, parks, waterside restaurants and traditional Konya cuisine; residential and calm, popular with families and locals escaping the city bustle.

A trendy, cafe-filled neighborhood in Selcuklu lined with restaurants, dessert shops and lively terraces; the city's most popular spot for eating out and evening strolls in an otherwise conservative city.

water.note: Tap is chlorinated but locals drink bottled; stick to cheap bottled water.

transit.hours: The tram runs roughly 6:00 AM to midnight; city buses cover similar hours with lighter late-night service.
transit.note: Konya's light-rail tram loops between the city center, Alaeddin Hill and the university/northern districts, backed by an extensive municipal bus network; the compact historic core is easily walkable.
transit.pay: Fares use the rechargeable ElKart / KonyaKart smart card, tapped on boarding trams and buses; single-ride cards are sold at kiosks and machines.

train: YHT high-speed rail to Ankara & Istanbul

transit.m: Municipal shuttle / city bus to the center (~30 min)
Taxi to the city center (25-30 min)

tip.r: Customary; leave around 10% at restaurants (bahsis) and round up taxi fares.

food.name: Etli ekmek
food.desc: Konya's metre-long flatbread spread thin with minced lamb, tomato and pepper and fired in a wood oven, then cut into strips.

places.name: Haci Sukru
places.note: One of the city's best-known etli ekmek ocakbasis, packed at lunchtime.

places.name: Pideci Hasan Sendagli
places.note: Open since 1985, five minutes' walk from the shrine; also famous for bicak arasi.

places.name: Somatci Fihi Ma Fih
places.note: Traditional Konya dishes with modern presentation; consistently top-rated by visitors.

food.name: Firin kebabi
food.desc: Fatty lamb slow-roasted for hours in a stone oven until it falls apart, served plain on flatbread with nothing but salt.

places.name: Haci Sukru
places.note: Roasts sell out by early afternoon - arrive between 11am and 1pm.

places.name: Kebapci Dedeler
places.note: Dating to 1929, one of Konya's oldest kebab houses, in the covered bazaar quarter.

places.name: Somatci Fihi Ma Fih
places.note: Reliable firin kebabi in a restored old house, good if you arrive late.

food.name: Tirit
food.desc: Torn flatbread soaked in lamb broth and layered with meat, yoghurt and hot butter - a dish the city eats standing up.

places.name: Tiritci Mithat
places.note: Specialist address widely rated the best tirit in Konya.

places.name: Somatci Fihi Ma Fih
places.note: Serves tirit alongside the rest of the classic Konya repertoire.

places.name: Bedesten esnaf lokantalari
places.note: Tradesmen's canteens in the covered market do cheap, honest tirit at noon.

food.name: Bamya corbasi
food.desc: Soup of tiny dried okra strung on threads, cooked with lamb and soured with lemon - a Konya wedding and holiday dish.

places.name: Somatci Fihi Ma Fih
places.note: One of the few places that keeps the old Mevlevi kitchen dishes on the daily menu.

places.name: Mevlevi Sofrasi
places.note: Ottoman-style dining room opposite the shrine, strong on soups and pilafs.

places.name: Bedesten esnaf lokantalari
places.note: Seasonal soup pots; ask what is cooking rather than reading the menu.

food.name: Sac arasi and Konya boregi
food.desc: Griddle breads folded around spiced meat, and paper-thin layered borek baked on a domed sac - the city's everyday snack food.

places.name: Pideci Hasan Sendagli
places.note: Bicak arasi from young beef sirloin is the house legend here.

places.name: Haci Sukru
places.note: Sac breads and pides fired alongside the etli ekmek.

places.name: Bedesten bazaar bakeries
places.note: Small ovens turning out borek and sac bread through the morning.

food.name: Hosmerim
food.desc: Warm pudding of fresh unsalted cheese and semolina, browned in butter and scattered with pistachio or walnut.

places.name: Somatci Fihi Ma Fih
places.note: Traditional Konya desserts served properly warm at the end of the meal.

places.name: Mevlevi Sofrasi
places.note: Old-style sweets including hosmerim and hoshaf near the Green Dome.

places.name: Bedesten sekerciler
places.note: Sweet shops in the covered market sell hosmerim and Konya's pismaniye to take away.

food.name: Ayran
food.desc: Salted yoghurt churned until foaming and served ice cold; in Konya it is the automatic partner to etli ekmek and firin kebabi.

places.name: Haci Sukru
places.note: House-churned ayran in copper bowls, poured the moment the bread arrives.

places.name: Pideci Hasan Sendagli
places.note: Foaming ayran by the jug, the way the locals order it.

places.name: Kebapci Dedeler
places.note: Century-old kebab house where ayran is the only drink most tables order.

food.name: Serbet and Turkish tea
food.desc: Chilled fruit and flower sherbets - rose, tamarind, liquorice - plus endless tulip glasses of tea; Konya is dry, so this is the toast.

places.name: Mevlevi Sofrasi
places.note: Serves classic Ottoman serbets alongside the food, opposite the shrine.

places.name: Somatci Fihi Ma Fih
places.note: House-made serbets rotate with the seasons.

places.name: Bedesten cay bahceleri
places.note: Tea gardens around the bazaar where a glass costs next to nothing.

landmarks: Mevlana Museum
Beneath its fluted turquoise dome rests the 13th-century Sufi poet Rumi, making this former dervish lodge Turkey's most visited spiritual shrine.
Whirling Dervish Sema Ceremony
At the Mevlana Cultural Centre, white-robed dervishes spin into mystical trance each Saturday, continuing the meditative ritual Rumi's order founded.
Alaeddin Mosque and Hill
Crowning the city's central mound, this sprawling 12th-century Seljuk mosque shelters sultans' tombs amid a forest of ancient recycled columns.
İnce Minareli Medrese
The extravagantly carved stone portal of this 1264 seminary, now a museum of Seljuk stonework, is a masterpiece of Islamic baroque exuberance.
Karatay Medrese
A 13th-century theological school turned tile museum, its dome of shimmering blue-and-gold star mosaics ranks among Seljuk art's supreme achievements.
Çatalhöyük
A day trip reaches this UNESCO-listed 9,000-year-old Neolithic settlement, one of humanity's earliest towns, with excavated houses and shrine murals.
Şems-i Tebrizi Mosque and Tomb
The serene shrine of Rumi's beloved spiritual mentor Shams of Tabriz draws pilgrims completing the Konya mystic circuit.
Aziziye Mosque
An unusual late-Ottoman mosque blending baroque and rococo flourishes, its illuminated twin minarets glow above the old bazaar quarter.
Sille Village
This ancient Greek village outside Konya preserves the frescoed Byzantine church of St. Helena, rock dwellings and stone bridges.
Sırçalı Medrese
A 1242 Seljuk seminary named for its glazed-tile courtyard iwan, now displaying carved tombstones in a tranquil open-air setting.

train.note: No international trains. Konya is on the YHT high-speed network, with fast trains to Ankara in about 1h45 and Istanbul in roughly 4h30, plus the overnight Meram Express. The high-speed station is a few kilometres from the centre with a tram connection. Book on TCDD e-bilet from 15 days out; trains fill during the December Şeb-i Arus Mevlana commemorations.

bus.note: No international coaches. Konya's otogar sits north of the centre on the tram line, with Kamil Koç (https://www.kamilkoc.com.tr/), Metro Turizm (https://www.metroturizm.com.tr/en) and Kontur running to Cappadocia (about 3 hours to Göreme), Antalya, Ankara and Istanbul. Book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/).

ferry.note: Konya is on the central Anatolian steppe with no coast or navigable river, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Sultanhanı Caravanserai
half.blurb: A 13th-century Seljuk caravanserai on the old Silk Road roughly 110 kilometers north of Konya, one of Anatolia's largest surviving stone way-stations.

half.name: Lake Tuz
half.blurb: Turkey's second-largest lake, a vast white salt flat northeast of Konya where visitors walk on the crust and flamingos gather in summer.

half.name: Beyşehir Lake
half.blurb: Turkey's largest freshwater lake southwest of Konya, ringed by the wooden-columned Eşrefoğlu Mosque and small fishing villages along its shore.

full.name: Cappadocia
full.blurb: A volcanic-rock region about 230 kilometers northeast of Konya with fairy-chimney formations, cave churches at Göreme, and the underground city of Kaymaklı.
